confirmed: Version: Scientific Reports 15, article 36987, published online 2025-10-22, CC BY-NC-ND 4.0. The Europe PMC JATS XML for PMC12546817 is the publisher's deposit, not an author manuscript (front matter; PMC metadata; Crossref). No PDF is on file, and the Nature HTML page returned a bot check, so the XML is the only full text; the form's version statement says this correctly.
Title and the five authors, in order, match the document (front matter).
Supplement 'no': PMC metadata flags no supplement, the paper cites none, and the Data availability text in 'where' is verbatim (back matter).

Design class and context class ai_vs_human: the first author ran 46 sessions of each chatbot, matched to each human's test order, item order, and AUT fluency (Methods, Procedure). The paper has no human-AI condition: 'we did not compare creativity task performance in grouped conditions, such as a human-human group or a human-GenAI group' (Discussion, limitations).
No randomized people study: only task order, AUT item order, and RAT item order were randomized (Methods, Procedure). With 46 people, the study would also fail the 50-person rule.

Counts: 46 people (Methods, Participants; Table 1, n = 46). The only removal reported is of invalid or incomplete AUT entries (ideas) before scoring (Methods, Scoring), and no person is reported as excluded, so n_analyzed 46 and n_randomized null are right. The Table 2 human fluency means (6.80, 7.30, 6.87) and the Table 4 human mean (19.13) are arithmetically consistent with n = 46.

46 sessions per model: 'An equal number of GenAI sessions were conducted for each chatbot, corresponding to the number of human participants' (Methods, Procedure). The RAT ANOVA reports F(2,135), which fits 3 x 46 sessions (Results, GenAI vs. GenAI).

Participants: the quote is verbatim; mean age 23.35 (SD 3.47); English not a first language for 13 (28.26%); McMaster University, Hamilton, Canada; convenience snowball sampling from any faculty (Methods, Participants; Table 1; affiliations).

AI tool: default parameters; tested Feb 16-17 (ChatGPT), Feb 17, 19, and 23 (DeepSeek), and Feb 17 (Gemini), 2025; the AUT prompt fixed the number of ideas to the matched human's fluency; only the title of each AI idea was scored (Methods, GenAI participants, Procedure, Scoring).
Task: shoe, tire, and pants at 3 min each; 57 RAT items with normative accuracy of 30 to 80% in 15 min; no timing in the AI prompts (Methods, Procedure).

Scoring and tests: Ocsai ocsai1-4o on a 1 to 5 scale; RAT answer key from ref. 32, Bowden and Jung-Beeman (2003), with spelling review; Wilcoxon signed-rank tests on fluency-matched pairs for the AUT and Student's t-tests for the RAT; three co-primary objectives (Introduction, The present study; Methods, Scoring, Statistical analysis).

S1-O1 'reported' matches Table 2 (human 2.96 (0.66), 3.27 (0.63), 3.20 (0.48); ChatGPT 3.77 (0.31), 4.23 (0.26), 4.11 (0.30)) and Table 3 (ChatGPT -0.800, -0.950, -0.900 with the stated 95% CIs, all < 0.001). The DeepSeek and Gemini values in measure_detail match Table 3. Differences are human minus AI (Table 3 footnote; Results text).

S1-O2 'reported' matches Table 2 (human 3.60 (0.55), 4.04 (0.53), 3.69 (0.58); ChatGPT 4.34 (0.24), 4.47 (0.19), 4.47 (0.16)) and Table 3 (ChatGPT -0.800, -0.550, -1.000 with the stated 95% CIs, all < 0.001). DeepSeek -0.500 (p = 0.005), -0.550, -0.500 and Gemini -0.650, -0.600, -0.750 in measure_detail match Table 3.

S1-O3 'reported' matches Table 4 (human 19.13 (9.96), range 2-42; ChatGPT 54.96 (0.89), range 53-56; *** p < 0.001 by Student's t-tests). DeepSeek 51.00 (1.59) and Gemini 44.93 (1.88) in measure_detail match Table 4.

One-line finding matches Table 3 (ChatGPT median-originality differences -0.800 to -0.950, p < 0.001), Table 4 (54.96 vs 19.13 of 57), and the abstract ('All GenAI models outperformed human participants in both tasks').

No company involvement: all authors are at McMaster University, 'The authors declare no competing interests', and the paper and Crossref state no funder (affiliations; Declarations). No data or code URL: raw data are available on request (Data availability).
summary: The short form for c029 is accurate: the paper compares 46 McMaster students with 46 matched sessions each of ChatGPT-4o, DeepSeek-V3, and Gemini 2.0 on the AUT and RAT, so it is ai_vs_human context and has no study that randomizes people to AI (only task and item order were randomized). Every reported number, the one-line finding, and the version statement match the Europe PMC JATS XML (Tables 2 to 4), and I found nothing to correct.
